Use this page when you plan which data a study needs, or meet a variable and
wonder where it comes from: a decision table from the question you have ("when
did this person die?") to the register and key columns that answer it, and a
table of the keys that link the registers. It assumes you can open and inspect
a register ([Phase 7 - Inspect your data](inspect-data.qmd)). When you know
which register to use, you find its exact column names, types and code
examples in [Overview of registers](register-reference.qmd), or search for a
single variable across all of them in [Find a variable](find-a-variable.qmd).

The table says which register covers what at DST (Statistics Denmark). Which of its columns and
years your project actually received was decided when the data was ordered, so
check your own delivery before you plan around anything here ([Check your
delivery](delivery-check.qmd)).

## Which register holds what {#what-am-i-looking-for---decision-table}

  | I want to find...                                    | Register                                    | Key column(s)                                                                                                                                                                |
  | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Date of birth and sex                                | BEF (the population register)                                         | `foed_dag`, `koen`                                                                                                                                                           |
  | Whether a person has died - and when                 | DOD (the register of deaths)                                         | `doddato`                                                                                                                                                                  |
  | Whether a person has emigrated                       | VNDS (the migration register)                                        | `haend_dato`, `indud_kode`                                                                                                                                                   |
  | A somatic hospital contact (until Feb/Mar 2019)      | lpr_adm                                     | `d_inddto`, `recnum`, `c_pattype`                                                                                                                                            |
  | A somatic diagnosis (until Feb/Mar 2019)             | lpr_diag                                    | `c_diag`, `c_diagtype`, `recnum`                                                                                                                                             |
  | A psychiatric diagnosis (e.g. schizophrenia, until Feb/Mar 2019) | t_psyk_adm + t_psyk_diag                    | `d_inddto`, `c_diag`, `c_diagtype`                                                                                                                                           |
  | A hospital contact or diagnosis (2019+)              | lpr_a_kontakt + lpr_a_diagnose              | `kont_starttidspunkt`, `diag_kode`, `diag_kode_type`                                                                                                                         |
  | A dispensed prescription                             | LMDB                                        | `atc`, `eksd`                                                                                                                                                                |
  | Education level                                      | UDDA                                        | `hfaudd`, `year`                                                                                                                                                              |
  | Household income                                     | FAIK (family income)                                        | `famaekvivadisp_13`, `familie_id`                                                                                                                                            |
  | Employment status                                    | AKM (the labour classification module)                                         | `socio13`, `year`                                                                                                                                                             |
  | An incident cancer diagnosis                         | The Danish Cancer Registry                  | `pnr` - see variable list                                                                                                                                                    |
  | A primary-sector contact (GP/specialist)             | National Health Insurance Service Register: sysi (older) / sssy (newer) | `pnr` - see variable list                                                                                                                                                    |
  | A laboratory result (e.g. HbA1c)                     | laboratorieproevesvar_                      | `pnr`, NPU (Nomenclature for Properties and Units, the code system for laboratory analyses) code, result value - column names differ between deliveries, see [Laboratory results](laboratory-results.qmd)                                 |
  | A surgical procedure / SKS (the Danish health care classification system) code                      | lpr_sksopr (LPR2) / project-specific (LPR3) | `c_opr`, `recnum` (LPR2) - LPR3: see [Overview of registers §5](register-reference.qmd)                                                                                      |
  | An examination / treatment (ZZ code)                 | lpr_sksube                                  | `recnum` - [see variable list](https://www.dst.dk/extranet/ForskningVariabellister/LPR_SKSUBE%20-%20Landspatientregistret%20-%20unders%C3%B8gelser%20og%20behandlinger.html) |
  | Birth outcomes / newborn facts (2019+)               | mfr_nyfoedte + 10 satellite tables          | `CPRnummer_Barn`, `CPRnummer_Mor` - see [Overview of registers §Nyfoedte](register-reference.qmd#mfr-nyfoedte)                                                              |
  | Birth outcomes / newborn facts (1997-2018)            | mfr                                         | `cpr_barn`, `cpr_moder` - see [Overview of registers §MFR (the Medical Birth Register)](register-reference.qmd#mfr---medical-birth-register)                                                             |
  | Birth outcomes / newborn facts (before 1997)          | ftbarn / ftforael / ftnaevn                 | `PNR` - see [Overview of registers §FTBARN (the child file of DST's fertility database)](register-reference.qmd#ftbarn)                                                                                                  |

Some diagnoses sit in both the somatic and the psychiatric register before 2019.
Dementia is the typical case: most dementia diagnoses are made in somatic
departments (neurology, geriatrics), so you need `lpr_diag` *and* `t_psyk_diag`.
The regions switched their reporting from LPR2 to LPR3 on 2-3 February or 2-3
March 2019, and DST's LPR2 files end on 31 March 2019 - see [Understanding
LPR (the National Patient Register)](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr-is-split-into-two-periods).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What are SKS codes?"}
**SKS** (Sundhedsvæsenets Klassifikations System, the Danish Health
Classification System) is the Danish health-care classification. It holds the
diagnosis codes, based on ICD-10, and the codes for operations and other
treatments in hospital, e.g. `KJDF10` for gastric bypass. The operation codes are
based on the Nordic NOMESCO Classification of Surgical Procedures (NCSP).
:::

## The socioeconomic registers come as a set

The three socioeconomic registers - UDDA (education), FAIK (income) and AKM
(employment) - are extracted together in [Socioeconomic
variables](socioeconomic-variables.qmd). One trap worth knowing before you start:
UDDA's `hfaudd` is a code for the *specific* education, **not** its level, so
getting a level out of it needs a lookup - see [Overview of
registers](register-reference.qmd#udda---education-register).

## Join keys

Wrong join keys produce silent errors: the code runs, but you lose rows - or
duplicate them.

  | Register                                                                                     | Join key        | Links to                                 |
  | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
  | BEF, DOD, VNDS, LMDB, UDDA, AKM, the Danish Cancer Registry, sysi/sssy, laboratorieproevesvar_ | `pnr`           | All other `pnr` registers                |
  | FAIK                                                                                         | `familie_id`    | Fetched from the BEF column `familie_id` |
  | `lpr_diag`                                                                                   | `recnum`        | `lpr_adm`                                |
  | `lpr_sksopr`                                                                                 | `recnum`        | `lpr_adm`                                |
  | `lpr_sksube`                                                                                 | `recnum`        | `lpr_adm`                                |
  | `lpr_a_diagnose`                                                                             | `dw_ek_kontakt` | `lpr_a_kontakt`                          |

Confirmed column names and join examples for each register are in [Overview of
registers](register-reference.qmd). The mechanics of joins are covered in [Phase
12 - Assemble and prepare the dataset](data-manipulation.qmd).
